inbox.message: I prefer linear_system because solving a 10x10 system with unique solution is straightforward using Gaussian elimination with exact fractions.
I prefer gram_determinant because computing a 6x6 Gram determinant from dot products of integer vectors is straightforward and yields an integer answer.
I prefer rank because it's straightforward row reduction to find pivot columns, and the output is a short list of integers.
I prefer change_of_basis because computing B^{-1} A B with integer matrices gives integer entries and is systematic.
I prefer qr because computing the QR decomposition via Gram-Schmidt on a 6x6 invertible matrix is systematic and yields rational numbers for the diagonal squared entries.
I prefer rref because computing the reduced row echelon form of an 8x10 matrix via Gaussian elimination is systematic and yields exact fractions.
I prefer projection because computing the orthogonal projection onto a subspace via solving the normal equations is systematic and yields exact fractions.
I prefer basis_coordinates because solving a 9x9 linear system for two vectors is systematic using Gaussian elimination with exact fractions.
I prefer least_squares because solving the normal equations yields a 6x6 linear system which is manageable and gives exact fractions.
